key_insight: A HIPAA-compliant LLM workflow can automatically phenotype rare hematologic malignancies from EHR data by combining retrieval, zero-shot text extraction, and clinician-guided conflict resolution.
clinical_relevance: This could make diagnosis and risk stratification for myeloproliferative neoplasms more scalable and more consistent across sites, beyond specialized tertiary centers.
method: Retrieved bone marrow biopsy reports, clinical notes, and structured labs from the EHR.
Used GPT-4 Turbo to extract diagnostic and prognostic variables from unstructured text.
Applied WHO/ICC diagnostic rules and NCCN-based risk models, with clinician-informed source prioritization to resolve conflicts.
evidence_signal: The held-out test set included 450 patients for diagnostic evaluation and 172 patients with clinical notes, with performance assessed against dual-clinician adjudicated ground truth using accuracy, F1, sensitivity, specificity, and kappa metrics.
watch_item: Real-world deployment will still depend on local data quality, documentation completeness, and careful validation when source records conflict or are sparse.
paper_title: Automated Phenotypic Characterization in Rare Hematologic Malignancies Using a Large Language Model-Based Framework
